_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: resource-sharing
description: Share hosts between agents and projects with claim files kept on each host (~/.solaris/claims/). tools/hostclaims.py (stdlib Python 3.8+, run on the controller, sent to each host over ssh as `python3 -`; no daemon, no central server, no root) claims cores, GPUs by index with a time-slicing share (P0 1.0, P1 0.5, P2/P3 0.25) and memory, RAM and disk under a flock so checking capacity and writing a claim are one step; counts unclaimed GPU processes, memory, RAM and CPU load as used and tags each host free, partly-busy or busy; launches jobs in tmux pinned with taskset and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, with a heartbeat, a done marker with the exit code, and release on exit; moves stale claims (old heartbeat and no process, or a changed boot id) to stale/ and keeps orphans; delivers yield requests to preemptible lower-priority jobs older than 20 minutes (TERM, then KILL after a grace); reports GPU-hours and CPU-hours per project; and keeps named shared counters with per-project caps for account-level limits. Projects in one Solaris tree share hosts through sharing links (resource-sharing.json: project slug and share_with), discovered automatically (a host is private to its owner until its list names others); every host has exactly one owner, acting only as its own project, who alone installs, renews, extends, maintains, releases or deletes it, while guests file (and may withdraw) extension, maintenance and release-objection requests the owner approves or declines. Lease kinds none, free and paid (paid cloud instances such as Brev: planned end, $/h, GPU type, instance); a fit command ranks existing hosts against launching a new instance (its wait and its dollars) and recommends reuse, reuse with an extension request, or launch new; an owner audit lists lease end, idle time, work outside claims, use by project, cost so far, open requests and a keep/extend/decline/release/delete/check recommendation, with a stricter idle limit for paid hosts and never a delete or release under running work. The skill covers setup, commands, priorities, ownership, fit, audit and pools; the always-on rule keeps jobs inside their claims, other projects' claims untouched, host changes with the owner, shared hosts from being deleted without the audit's advice (guarding other plugins' teardowns), and paid instances from being extended on one's own or left idle.

notes: List the project's hosts in <pack>/.memory/hosts.json as [{name, target, opts}] (target user@address, opts the ssh options), with an optional owner (project slug) and lease ({kind: none|free|paid, planned_end, usd_per_hour, gpu_type, instance}).

To share hosts with other projects in this Solaris tree, create <pack>/.memory/resource-sharing.json: {"project": "<slug>", "share_with": ["<other-slug>"]} (an optional policy block holds weights, class defaults, fit and audit thresholds). Hosts that other projects share with this one are merged in automatically. Without the file, this project's hosts stay private to it.

For each host this project owns, run `python3 <pack>/plugins/resource-sharing/tools/hostclaims.py install --host <name>` from the project root (hosts need Python 3.8+, tmux and taskset), and record the footprint ~/.solaris/claims/ on that host in <pack>/.memory/resources.md. Owners run `audit` at least every two hours (hourly for paid hosts) and delete or release a shared host only on its advice.
